definitions.explanation: A heavy outer garment worn over other clothing for warmth. A somewhat literary or old-fashioned word, now largely replaced by コート in everyday speech.

examples.japanese: {外套|がいとう}を{羽織|はお}る。
{寒|さむ}さに{耐|た}えかねて{外套|がいとう}の{襟|えり}を{立|た}てた。
examples.english: Unable to bear the cold, he turned up the collar of his overcoat.

examples.japanese: {玄関|げんかん}に{掛|か}けてあった{黒|くろ}い{外套|がいとう}を{手|て}に{取|と}り、{夜|よる}の{街|まち}へ{出|で}た。
examples.english: He picked up the black overcoat hanging in the entryway and went out into the night streets.

notes:
A literary compound of {外|がい} (outer) + {套|とう} (covering/sheath). More commonly encountered in literature, period dramas, and historical writing than in everyday conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {外套|がいとう}を{着|き}る: to wear an overcoat
- {外套|がいとう}を{脱|ぬ}ぐ: to take off an overcoat
- {外套|がいとう}を{羽織|はお}る: to throw on an overcoat
- {軍用|ぐんよう}{外套|がいとう}: military overcoat

SIMILAR WORDS:
- コート: coat — the standard modern word for coats and overcoats
- オーバー: overcoat — older loanword (from 'overcoat'), still used by older speakers
- マント: mantle, cape — a cloak-style outer garment

LITERARY NOTE:
{外套|がいとう} is the Japanese title of Gogol's famous short story "The Overcoat." The word evokes a literary, atmospheric quality.
